text:
opalstream_prod: Hey team — since 22:00 UTC our production pool on Dedicated (region-us-west) saw a sustained burst ~2.3x baseline TPS, clients started getting 429s and we see burst credits dropped to 0.0. Can we triage?
sam_support: Thanks for flagging — looking now. Can you paste the request pattern / any ramp script?
opalstream_prod: Pattern is batch invoice summarization calls, many 8k-token prompts in parallel. We pushed a marketing batch ~21:50 UTC hitting an unexpected steady rate rather than a short spike. No auth errors, just 429s + higher p99 latency.
lex_sre: Gathering admission controller logs + pool metrics. Initial glance: admission headroom fell below threshold and fallback model routing triggered.
maya_oncall: @lex_sre paste the admission controller output here if you have it. Also what are their reserved/dedicated limits?
opalstream_prod: They have a Dedicated pool with 12 GPUs reserved, configured burst credits = 120k tokens, autoscale min=12 max=20.
lex_sre: Log snippets: ``[2025-03-12T22:07:41Z] admission: pool=dedicated-usw-opa; tps=4800; headroom=0.2; burst_credits=0.0; admit=threshold_reached; action=throttle`` ``[2025-03-12T22:08:12Z] routing: fallback=model-small-quant; reason=admit_failure; latency_increase=+120ms``
infra-bot: Deploy alert: dedicated-autoscaler scaled from 12 -> 12 (no scaling) due to scaling cooldown. Recent scale attempts suppressed by cooldown policy.
jordan_engineer: That cooldown is 10m after a downscale and 2m after an upscale, configured in their pool policy. If they had a rapid ramp we'd need more aggressive rules or pre-warming.
sam_support: Billing note — burst credits reported 0 on our side; we need to confirm whether credits decayed earlier or were consumed. @billing_ops can you confirm credit accounting?
billing_ops: Looking. Usage ledger shows heavy token consumption starting 21:51 UTC for ~17 minutes: delta=125,300 tokens. Prior balance 120,000 -> exhausted at 21:59. There was a small decay applied per policy at 20:00 (-2k). We charged consumption; no billing inconsistency.
lex_sre: Repro attempt: I replayed a scaled-down client load hitting same sequence (8 concurrent heavy requests per client) against a staging replica. With pool config identical I reproduced admission throttling after credits exhausted. Autoscaler did not react because the average CPU/GPU utilization metric threshold didn't cross the upscale trigger within the cooldown window.
maya_oncall: Can we get p99 latency and queue length graphs?
lex_sre: p99 token latency jumped from 90ms to 220ms during fallback routing; queue length spiked to 40 in-flight queued requests. Admission token-rate buckets saturated.
opalstream_prod: For mitigation, can you temporarily whitelist traffic or bump credits? We need to keep client jobs running — they are business-critical.
jordan_engineer: Short-term options: 1) Manual credit top-up (support action) 2) Temporary pool horizontal scale (increase max to 30 and force scale) 3) Adjust cooldown to allow immediate scale-up (risky) 4) Enable graceful reject earlier to avoid fallback model and p99 regressions.
sam_support: Which do they want?
opalstream_prod: Please top-up credits ASAP and allow us to finish the batch. We'll follow with a config change.
illing_error: (system) -- not a real participant -- ignore
billing_ops: Done: issued 50k extra burst credits at 22:15 UTC. New balance 50,000. Please monitor.
infra-bot: Autoscaler action: manual_scale requested by jordan_engineer -> target=20; override applied at 22:18 UTC. Pool now at 20 GPUs.
opalstream_prod: Confirming requests are flowing, 429s dropping. Thanks. We'll throttle the client ramp to finish remaining jobs.
maya_oncall: Postmortem notes: root cause = tight cooldown + credit buffer too low for this workload pattern (long wide batch instead of short spike). Secondary factor = fallback routing to smaller model increased p99 but did not prevent admission failures.
lex_sre: Action items: - (lex_sre) add admission metric that accounts for token-length-weighted TPS for triggering scale - (jordan_engineer) propose new cooldown policy for burst-prone customers (reduce upscale cooldown to 30s, increase downscale to 10m) - (billing_ops) recommend default burst credit safety margin for long-running batch jobs - (sam_support) document emergency top-up playbook and auto-topup option in console
opalstream_prod: We'll update our job scheduler to add linear ramp (max 1.2x per minute) and target smaller model variants where quality acceptable.
jordan_engineer: For longer-term: consider prewarm API for scheduled batches + commitment-based burst credit add-ons.
sam_support: I'll follow up with a ticket and add runbook steps. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
opalstream_prod: Thanks all — we'll reach out if anything recurs.
